title: Geometric norm projection by finite supported-lattice devissage
statement:
Fix distinct primes $p,\ell$, a field $k$ of characteristic $p$, a separable closure $k^s$, and a separated finite-type $k$-scheme $X$. Put $T=X\times_k k^s$ and let $u:T\to X$ be projection. Fix a normed algebraic closure $\Omega/\mathbf Q_\ell$ and a finite intermediate field $E$, with the restricted norm. On profinite sets set $A(P)=C(P,E)$ and $B(P)=C(P,\Omega)$, using all continuous maps [def-sfb-continuous-map-condensed-ring]. Put $R_Z=p_Z^*R$ for $R=A,B$ and $Z=X,T$, use internal modules, ordinary derived categories and K-flat derived tensor [sk-def-sfb-pulled-back-coefficients, sk-def-sfb-module-objects, sk-def-sfb-derived-categories, sk-def-sfb-derived-tensor-hom]. Let $V\in D(\operatorname{Mod}_{A_X})$ be bounded constructible in the finite constant local model convention [sk-def-sfb-constructible], and put $V^s=u^*V$ using the module pullback [sk-def-sfb-module-derived-pushpull].

The complex $V^s$ belongs to $\Dbc(T,E)$ in that same convention. It belongs to the subcategory obtained by finitely many cones and integer shifts from the supported lattice objects
$$Q=(i_!L_0)[1/\ell]=A_T\otimes_{O_T}i_!L_0,$$
where $O(P)=C(P,\mathcal O_E)$, $\mathcal O_E=\{x\in E:|x|\leq1\}$, $i:S\hookrightarrow T$ is constructible locally closed and $L_0$ is a lisse finite-rank $O_S$-module [def-weil-l-adic-coefficient-extension, def-sfb-lisse-coefficient-module]; $i_!$ is open extension by zero followed by closed pushforward [lem-weil-pbc-condensed-open-closed-recollement]. Writing $\mathcal H_R=Rp_{T*,R}$ for derived geometric sections to condensed $R$-modules [sk-def-sfb-pullback-from-point, sk-def-sfb-module-derived-pushpull], the specified coefficient projection
$$\pi_{V^s}:B\otimes_A^L\mathcal H_A(V^s)\longrightarrow\mathcal H_B(B_T\otimes_{A_T}^LV^s)$$
is an isomorphism in $D(\operatorname{Mod}_B)$. Here $\pi_N$ is the transpose under $B\otimes_A^L-\dashv\operatorname{Res}$ of $\mathcal H_A(N)\to\operatorname{Res}\mathcal H_B(B_T\otimes^L_{A_T}N)$ induced by the scalar unit $n\mapsto1\otimes n$ and the canonical comparison with exact restriction. These maps are natural in $N$ and commute with the canonical shifts and connecting morphisms of distinguished triangles. The assertion includes empty $X$ and $V=0$ and assumes neither completeness of $\Omega$ nor flatness of $A\to B$.

proof.text: Base change of the separated finite-type structure morphism along $\operatorname{Spec}k^s\to\operatorname{Spec}k$ makes $T$ separated and finite type over $k^s$. Both $X$ and $T$ are qcqs. The field $k^s$ is separably closed of characteristic $p\ne\ell$, so it is an allowed standing base field for finite-$E$ lattice generation and for the supported norm-projection theorem. No finite-type hypothesis on $u:T\to X$ is needed.

Exactness of module inverse image and its exact termwise derived factorization give $H^q(u^*V)\cong u^*H^q(V)$. Thus the same finite cohomological interval bounds $V^s$. Apply finite-constant-model pullback to each $H^q(V)$ with coefficient $\underline E=A$: its pulled strata and covers, with the same finitely presented $E$-modules, give constructibility on $T$. Hence $V^s\in\Dbc(T,E)$ in precisely the asserted convention.

source.place: Exactness and sums; Constructible complexes, finite-E case.

proof.text: Apply clause (1) of integral-model generation over the standing field $k^s$ to $V^s$. It gives a finite cone-and-shift expression with leaves $(i_!L_0)[1/\ell]=A_T\otimes_{O_T}i_!L_0$. These are the generators in the question: the coefficients are the pulled-back norm-topological $E$ and $\mathcal O_E$, and lisse means pro-etale locally finite free, allowing variable rank and zero. A field is Noetherian since its only ideals are zero and the unit ideal; finite type therefore makes $T$ Noetherian, so closed subsets of its underlying space satisfy the minimal condition, equivalently the descending-chain condition. Every subset of its underlying space is therefore quasi-compact. In particular opens and complements of closed subsets are quasi-compact opens; their intersections show that every locally closed stratum in that theorem is constructible. The convention for $i_!$ is the exact open-then-closed extension used there; the stated recollement functors give this convention for our bounded-below generators.

source.place: Clause (1), finite-E supported integral lattice generation.

proof.text: Put $s=\operatorname{Spec}k^s$ and $t:T\to s$. Apply scalar-mate thick closure to $t$ and $A_s\to B_s$. Its $\beta_{t,N}$ is the counit mate; after exact scalar restriction it is the specified projection transformation, with its canonical shift and connecting squares. Field/action derived-section transport over $k^s$, taking its separable closure to be itself, has trivial Galois group. It identifies $D(E_R)Rt_{*,R}$ with $\mathcal H_R$ and identifies this counit mate with the scalar-unit-transpose $\pi_N$ in the question. The equivalences preserve scalar units, restriction, input morphisms and shifts; since they are exact, their termwise derived functors preserve distinguished triangles. Therefore $\pi$ is natural and its components form morphisms of distinguished triangles, including the connecting squares. Invertibility is preserved and reflected by these equivalences, so the isomorphism locus for $\pi_N$ contains zero and is closed under isomorphisms, all integer shifts and cones. This argument uses ordinary K-flat tensor and exact scalar restriction, with no flatness of $A\to B$.

source.place: Paragraph (3), agent-extracted formal geometric coefficient-projection assembly; trivial-Galois specialization of existing field/action transport and thick-locus statements.

proof.text: For every leaf $Q$ in step 3 apply supported-lattice norm projection with $K=k^s$, the same $E\subset\Omega$, the same immersion into $T$, and the same $L_0$. Its map is expressly the transpose of the scalar unit followed by the exact restriction comparison, hence is exactly $\pi_Q$, not merely an unspecified isomorphism of its source and target. Thus every leaf lies in the locus of step 4.

source.place: Paragraph (3), agent-extracted supported-lattice norm projection obligation; reuse the existing supported-lattice theorem, not a claim that the paragraph proves it.

proof.text: Induct on the finite cone-and-shift expression of step 3. The leaves satisfy the assertion by step 5, zero does by step 4, and shifting or replacing an object by an isomorphic one preserves it by step 4. At a cone node the two already constructed components of the morphism of distinguished triangles from step 4 are invertible; two-out-of-three for triangle morphisms makes the third component invertible. This proves that $\pi_{V^s}$ is invertible. The naturality and shift/connecting compatibility were proved for all $N$ in step 4 and therefore apply to $V^s$. If $V=0$ or $X$ is empty, then $V^s=0$; both functors take it to zero and its unique comparison is the zero-object isomorphism. None of these steps completes $\Omega$ or replaces all continuous functions by finite-subextension-valued functions.
